thesis: QNX is for predictable capture deadlines, failure containment, restart/recovery, and inspectable scheduling under load, not model accuracy or raw inference speed.

claims.summary: Physical QNX 8.0.0 runs on a Raspberry Pi 5 (aarch64le) and accepts the SSH runner.
The final laptop 320 NCNN model executed through the native NCNN path on the Pi.
Ten model-only inference samples measured on the Pi: mean 98.4287 ms (~10.16 FPS).
ONNX-vs-QNX synthetic parity: max abs 0.000732421875, mean abs 0.000013902, p99 0.0001602936.
A real feces frame ran through the final native NCNN model on the Pi in 100.583 ms and matched the ONNX reference closely.
The native NCNN paths are Pi-local and experimental; they are not production deployments.
Final NCNN artifacts are content-addressed by SHA-256.
QNX fixed-priority scheduling is OS-supported but not yet configured in this project.
SCHED_SPORADIC is OS-supported for capping inference execution time but not yet configured.
HAM (High Availability Manager) is planned for detecting and restarting failed workers; it is not instrumented yet.
Hardware watchdog recovery is planned; it is not instrumented yet.
QNX kernel tracing is planned; it is not instrumented yet.
Capture jitter and deadline metrics are planned; they are not instrumented yet.
Separating capture, inference, and publisher into distinct services is planned; it is not instrumented yet.
QNX 8 does not support the Adaptive Partitioning Scheduler; no APS or adaptive CPU partition is claimed, configured, or active.
